newsitem.title: UK: LME rocked by spec sales, most markets end down.
newsitem.headline: LME rocked by spec sales, most markets end down.

text.p: Base metal markets were hit by a wave of speculative selling during Tuesday afternoon LME trading, and with sentiment soft in copper, several were bruised at the close.

Traders said the decline in copper was par for the course as the market is suffering from the summer slowdown, rising stocks and a move back into a cash/threes contango. Losses in aluminium and zinc were somewhat surprising, given current tightness.
But traders said the speculative selling spree, and the way it spilt over into other markets, was only to be expected.
"It is just the way it is - the funds are prowling around at the moment," one said.
Copper was hard hit, falling to the lowest levels since December 1996, trading at $2,118 a tonne, showing a loss of nearly eight percent from levels that prevailed only last Thursday.
Key support held at $2,120, however, and by the close prices had clawed back some lost ground. Last trade was at $2,145, still down $17 a tonne from Monday.
Aluminium was slapped by fund selling as investment interests who bought metal when prices were rising from $1,600 a few weeks ago opted to take profits.
The market managed to hold $1,630, but still ended at $1,634, down $43 from yesterday.

The fall took some by surprise, given the flare-up earlier in nearby premiums. This morning, the backwardation to borrow "tom/next" metal (belated business against the previous day's prompt date) leapt to $21 as shorts were forced to cover.
Cash/threes touched $60 at one stage, but eased back to $35/45 this afternoon, with some lending seen against further forward months.

LME authorities monitored the dealings this morning without taking any action. "The August date was the key date in aluminium, so we're watching how it performed," LME Chief Executive David King said.
Aluminium stocks fell today by 425 tonnes, but inventories are likely to increase in coming weeks as metal is drawn in by the backwardation, traders said.
Zinc buckled during the afternoon when copper came under pressure, with liquidation driving the market down to a $1,461 low.
A subsequent bounce helped cut losses, although final trade was at $1,477, still down $15.
Cash/threes was at a slightly softer backwardation of $153/158, but the September tightness will continue to make the market nervous, traders said.
Nickel was also rebuffed during the afternoon, and the current technical bounce is showing signs of running out of steam now. Last business was at an unchanged $6,670.
Lead hardly moved throughout the session, and appears immune to developments elsewhere. Prices are ranging above $600, with last trade today at $603, down $7.
Tin was also a passive onlooker to the main trend, with prices fluctuating quietly close to overnight levels. Last trade was at an unchanged $5,370.
Alloy moved lower with primary prices, and was indicated some $30 easier at $1,470/75.
--Martin Hayes, London Newsroom 44 171 542 8080
